question: Should OpenClaw require exact account and thread evidence before accepting threaded ACP/subagent completion delivery, even when older integrations may emit partial target metadata?
rationale: This is a deliberate compatibility and message-delivery contract choice; source-level tests can demonstrate the selected predicate but cannot decide which existing metadata omissions must remain accepted.

options.title: Adopt strict threaded matching
options.body: Merge only after current-head proof confirms wrong-target outcomes fall back to the requester route while exact account/thread evidence still succeeds.

options.title: Preserve broader compatibility
options.body: Retain acceptance for selected partial target evidence and document the narrow cases where explicit mismatches still fail.

options.title: Split the contract decision
options.body: Land outbound target serialization separately and defer completion-accounting strictness until owners agree on the long-term evidence contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict threaded matching
recommendation.body: Merge only after current-head proof confirms wrong-target outcomes fall back to the requester route while exact account/thread evidence still succeeds.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged route-account-bound work is the closest available current history signal for deciding cross-account target matching.
